thread.title: Asia Markets: Asian stocks drop as tech pullback, Nissan CEO’s arrest takes toll

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Asia Markets: Asian stocks drop as tech pullback, Nissan CEO’s arrest takes toll
text:
Asian stock markets fell in early trading Tuesday, following tech-led declines on Wall Street.
Japan’s Nikkei
 NIK, -1.08%
 was down 0.8%, with electronics and machinery stocks among the biggest decliners. Sony
 6758, -2.67%
 was down 2.6% while Fanuc
 6954, -2.84%
 and Hitachi
 6501, -3.23%
 were off some 3%. But the auto sector was the most watched, following the arrest of Nissan CEO Carlos Ghosn on Monday. Alliance partners Nissan
 7201, -5.05%
 and Mitsubishi
 7211, -6.85%
 slid in early trading, with Nissan at almost-2½-year lows. But rival Toyota
 7203, +1.85%
 benefited, climbing 2%.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index
 HSI, -1.87%
 fell 1.3%, with Tencent
 0700, -3.30%
 down 2.5% and smartphone-component firms AAC
 2018, -3.30%
 and Sunny Optical
 2382, -3.03%
 off some 2%. Xiaomi
 1810, +4.12%
 jumped 5% after its third-quarter earnings report
In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite
 SHCOMP, -1.63%
 was down 1.2% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite
 399106, -1.77%
 dropped 1.4%. Among large caps, real estate was off 1.3% after yesterday’s sharp bounce. Financials, which also were strong Monday, pulled back 0.9%.
A report about another round of production cuts for iPhones weighed on Apple
 AAPL, -3.96%
 suppliers in Asia. Taiwan’s Taiex
 Y9999, -0.93%
 fell 0.5% as product assembler Hon Hai
 2317, -3.00%
 dropped 2.7% to hit fresh five-year lows and Taiwan Semiconductor
 2330, -1.58%
 declined 1.3%. Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix
 000660, -3.01%
 slid another 2.7% and Samsung Electronics
 005930, -2.06%
 lost 1.7% as the Kospi
 SEU, -0.99%
 dropped 0.6%.
Australia’s benchmark index
 XJO, -0.79%
 was down 0.8%, and New Zealand
 NZ50GR, -1.17%
 and Singapore
 STI, -1.24%
 posted losses as well.
